setup: SPRAT is open in a web browser within a requirements workshop where analysts, project managers, and an administrator are collaborating on a web-system privacy review.
action: A team member opens an existing project that contains goals, scenarios, policies, requirements, and compliance references for the web system.
expected_observation: The project workspace presents these artifacts together in a shared collaborative workbench, allowing participants to review and align requirements with privacy and security policies in the same environment.

setup: A project already contains multiple goals, scenario descriptions, policy statements, requirement records, and compliance references entered by different team members.
action: An analyst navigates to the project's consolidated workspace to review the current analysis.
expected_observation: The system displays the related goals, scenarios, policies, requirements, and compliance information in a centralized view with traceable links between items, supporting consistent reasoning across the project.

setup: The organization uses a document repository for requirements documents and an issue-tracking tool for change requests and review comments, alongside SPRAT.
action: A project manager opens a project in SPRAT after importing or referencing the existing documents and issue items used by the team.
expected_observation: SPRAT operates as part of the existing workflow by allowing the project to be reviewed alongside document and issue-tracking references without forcing the team to abandon their established tools and processes.

setup: A new SPRAT project is available with user accounts created for an administrator, a project manager, an analyst, and a guest.
action: Each of the four users signs in to the system using their assigned account.
expected_observation: The system recognizes each role and presents access and available actions appropriate to administrator, project manager, analyst, and guest users.

setup: An administrator is signed in and the user management area contains accounts with varying access levels.
action: The administrator opens the access control settings and modifies a user's project permissions.
expected_observation: The system allows the administrator to manage system settings and user access, including changing permissions or account access within the bounds of administrative authority.

setup: A project manager is signed in to a project that already contains submitted analyses and review items.
action: The project manager opens the project review dashboard to inspect the current work.
expected_observation: The system allows the project manager to oversee the project, review submitted work, and view the project's analysis status and associated artifacts.

setup: An analyst is signed in to an active project with editable requirement and policy mapping records.
action: The analyst creates a new requirement entry and updates its mapping to a policy statement.
expected_observation: The system permits the analyst to create and update requirements and policy mappings, and the changes are saved and reflected in the project record.

setup: A guest account is signed in to a project that contains requirements, policies, and analysis results.
action: The guest opens the project workspace and attempts to review the available information.
expected_observation: The system provides read-only access to permitted project information and prevents the guest from creating, editing, approving, or deleting any records.

setup: An analyst is working in a project workspace where no content has yet been entered for a new privacy analysis.
action: The analyst creates a goal, adds a scenario, records a policy reference, defines a requirement, and attaches a compliance reference to the same project.
expected_observation: The system stores all captured goals, scenarios, policies, requirements, and compliance references and displays them as project artifacts available for later review and traceability.

setup: A goal has been recorded in a project and one or more source policies have already been entered in the policy library.
action: The analyst opens the goal record and links it to its originating policy statement.
expected_observation: The system shows the trace from the goal back to the source policy, allowing the policy-to-goal relationship to be reviewed from the goal record.

setup: Two analysts have independently completed analyses for the same project, each with their own sets of traced goals, policies, and requirements.
action: The project manager selects both analysts' analyses and requests a comparison.
expected_observation: The system produces a comparison view that lets the project manager compare the two analyses against each other, highlighting similarities and differences between them.

setup: Two alternative analysis sets exist in the same project, each containing aligned goals, policies, and requirement mappings.
action: An analyst chooses the side-by-side compare option for those two analysis sets.
expected_observation: The system displays both analyses next to each other in a side-by-side layout so the analyst can inspect corresponding items directly.

setup: Two analysts have traced the same goal in a project, but one linked it to Policy A while the other linked it to Policy B, and their resulting requirements differ.
action: A project manager opens the comparison view for the two analyses.
expected_observation: The system clearly flags the conflicting trace choices and the differing requirements, showing that the same goal was traced to different policies or produced different requirement outcomes.

setup: A disputed item exists in the project, such as a requirement or policy mapping that analysts have not yet agreed on.
action: An analyst opens the disputed item and adds a comment or discussion note directly on that record.
expected_observation: The system attaches the comment or discussion note to the specific disputed item so the conversation remains linked to the exact requirement, policy, or analysis entry.

setup: The project glossary has been configured with approved terms and their definitions for use across the workspace.
action: An analyst enters a requirement or policy statement using a term that already exists in the controlled vocabulary.
expected_observation: The system recognizes the shared glossary term and presents the approved meaning, encouraging consistent terminology across goals, scenarios, policies, and requirements.

setup: An analyst is editing a requirements artifact that contains a glossary field, and the term dictionary already includes an approved definition for the entered term.
action: The analyst types a known term into the term entry field.
expected_observation: The system displays the accepted definition for that term alongside the entry field, using the approved wording from the glossary.

setup: An analyst is creating a new glossary term while the system already contains an existing term with very similar wording and another requirement uses the new term differently from the approved definition.
action: The analyst enters the new term and saves the entry.
expected_observation: The system warns that the term is too close to an existing term or is being used inconsistently, and the warning identifies the conflicting term or usage.

setup: The analyst is entering terms into a requirements artifact, and the glossary contains approved terms, near matches, and a known duplicate candidate.
action: The analyst continues typing a term that matches or nearly matches an existing glossary entry, or uses the term in a context that conflicts with its approved definition.
expected_observation: The system checks the term during entry and flags likely duplicates, near matches, or uses that do not fit the approved definition without waiting for the form to be fully submitted.

setup: The analyst is typing a term into a live entry field on an active requirements form.
action: The analyst enters a term that triggers a glossary warning while continuing to edit the same line.
expected_observation: A warning appears immediately near the term entry field, but the rest of the form remains usable and the analyst can continue working without a modal interruption.

setup: The system has shown a warning for a term that may be a duplicate or a near match, and the analyst is still in the term-editing workflow.
action: The analyst chooses one of the available responses: reuse the existing term, revise the term text, or add a clarification note.
expected_observation: The system accepts the selected response and updates the term entry accordingly, preserving the analyst's choice without discarding the current work.

setup: An analyst is entering a term that already exists in the project glossary and has prior usage history, source notes, or contextual references.
action: The analyst focuses the term field or starts typing the term.
expected_observation: The system shows the existing context for that term during entry, including relevant prior usage or associated notes, so the analyst can judge whether the term is appropriate.

setup: An analyst is entering artifact metadata and term content in a form that validates terms as they are added.
action: The analyst attempts to enter a clearly disallowed value, such as an empty required term field or a value explicitly blocked by policy.
expected_observation: The system presents a hard error that prevents completion of the invalid action and clearly indicates that the entry is not allowed.

setup: An analyst enters a term that is close to a glossary term but not an exact match, or uses wording that is potentially ambiguous but not prohibited.
action: The analyst saves or advances the artifact with that term still present.
expected_observation: The system shows a softer warning rather than a blocking error, indicating the term may be a duplicate, ambiguous, or not an exact glossary match.

setup: A term-entry warning is displayed for a term that has approved alternatives and historical examples in the repository.
action: The analyst opens the suggestion details for the warning.
expected_observation: The system provides approved alternative terms and examples of prior usage so the analyst can compare the options before deciding how to proceed.

setup: The system is showing a suggested approved term in response to a warning, and the analyst is reviewing the suggestion inline.
action: The analyst clicks the one-click accept control for the suggested term.
expected_observation: The suggested term is inserted or replaced immediately in the entry field, and the warning is cleared or updated to reflect the accepted term.

setup: An analyst is creating or editing an artifact record in a project workspace that supports structured metadata.
action: The analyst enters rationale, source notes, assumptions, and a status value for the artifact, then saves the record.
expected_observation: The artifact stores and displays the rationale, source notes, assumptions, and status as persistent metadata fields.

setup: The analyst has access to multiple analysis cases within the tool, and artifacts already belong to different projects or cases.
action: The analyst opens the artifact list for a selected project or analysis case.
expected_observation: Only artifacts associated with the chosen project or analysis case are grouped together in that view, while artifacts from other cases remain separated.

setup: An artifact repository contains classification fields for system, stakeholder, and policy source, and at least one artifact has values for these categories.
action: The analyst filters or browses artifacts by one of these organizing dimensions, such as system or stakeholder.
expected_observation: The system groups or filters artifacts according to the selected dimension, making artifacts from the chosen system, stakeholder, or policy source easy to locate.

setup: An artifact exists in the workspace and the analyst has permissions to change its lifecycle state.
action: The analyst updates the artifact state from draft to review, approved or accepted, or archived.
expected_observation: The artifact reflects the selected lifecycle state, and the state shown in the UI matches one of the supported states: draft, review, approved or accepted, or archived.

setup: An artifact has an existing history of prior revisions, and audit/comparison access is enabled in the workspace.
action: The analyst opens the version history or compares the current artifact with an earlier revision.
expected_observation: Older versions remain accessible and traceable, with version identifiers, timestamps, or revision history visible for audit and comparison.

setup: An archived policy item exists in the system with an assigned archive date, policy number, and linked review history, and the current user has permission to search compliance records.
action: The user searches the repository using the archived policy number and opens the archived item from the search results.
expected_observation: The archived item appears in search results, can be opened, and displays its archive status, trace history, and related references without being excluded from search.

setup: A policy record is already approved and locked for direct edits, and a reviewer account has permission to add review comments and change suggestions.
action: The reviewer opens the approved record, adds a comment, and submits a suggested change to the wording of a control statement.
expected_observation: The reviewer's comment and suggestion are saved as review annotations, while the approved record remains unchanged until an authorized revision is separately accepted.

setup: A guest account has been created for the system with read-only permissions and no edit, approve, or export privileges.
action: The guest signs in and opens a policy record, then attempts to modify the content or submit a status change.
expected_observation: The guest can view the record and its metadata, but edit controls are unavailable or rejected, and no changes are applied to the record.

setup: Two users have overlapping access to the same policy draft, and one user has already made unsaved changes to a section that the second user also edited.
action: The second user tries to save their edits to the same section and finalize the update.
expected_observation: The system detects the overlapping edit, warns the user before final submission, and prevents the change from being finalized until the conflict is reviewed.

setup: A policy record contains trace links to supporting evidence and references to an external policy that has been deleted from the repository.
action: A compliance analyst opens the record's traceability view or runs a trace integrity check.
expected_observation: The system flags the broken trace link and identifies the record as pointing to a deleted policy, with the affected reference clearly marked for follow-up.

setup: The system has detected a data consistency issue affecting a policy record during validation or synchronization, and a recovery copy exists in the recovery store.
action: The user opens the affected record after the consistency warning is raised.
expected_observation: The record remains recoverable, the user is offered a restoration or recovery path, and the original content is not lost or permanently overwritten.

setup: A record is in conflict resolution mode after multiple edits, and the system has audit data for the latest successful update.
action: The user opens the conflict details panel for the record.
expected_observation: The system shows the identity of the last person who changed the record and a summary of what was changed, including the affected fields or sections.

setup: A policy item has an unresolved conflict between two versions and is available for reviewer action.
action: The reviewer starts the conflict resolution process from the item's conflict alert.
expected_observation: The system launches a guided workflow that steps the reviewer through reviewing differences, choosing a resolution option, and confirming the outcome.

setup: Two conflicting versions of the same record exist, and the conflict resolution screen is available to the reviewer.
action: The reviewer opens the comparison view for the conflicting versions.
expected_observation: Both versions are displayed side by side, and the changed text, fields, or values are visibly highlighted so the reviewer can identify exact differences.

setup: A record conflict has been created involving an author, a reviewer, and a compliance approver listed as participants in the item.
action: The conflict is submitted for resolution.
expected_observation: The involved people receive notifications about the conflict, and the notification includes the record identifier and a prompt to review or respond.

setup: A conflict exists on a policy record and the conflict resolution screen is open to a reviewer.
action: The reviewer adds notes explaining the preferred resolution and replies within the conflict discussion area.
expected_observation: A comment thread or notes area is available, the reviewer's notes are saved, and the discussion remains attached to the conflict record for later review.

setup: A policy record is in conflict, and the reviewer has permission to resolve, retain, or reopen the item depending on the conflict severity and review outcome.
action: The reviewer chooses an appropriate resolution option such as merging the content, keeping one version, or reopening the item for further review.
expected_observation: The system offers the available resolution path appropriate to the situation, applies the selected outcome, and updates the item status accordingly without losing the unresolved alternatives when reopening is chosen.

setup: A source policy document and related supporting files are available in an external document repository, and the importing user has access to that repository connection.
action: The user starts an import of the source policy and selects the supporting files to bring into the system.
expected_observation: The system imports the selected source policy and supporting files from the repository and creates corresponding records or attachments in the target workspace.

setup: A policy migration is in progress from a document repository where the source document includes author, created and modified timestamps, ownership information, trace links, and a classification that can be mapped directly.
action: The user completes the migration/import of the source policy into the new system.
expected_observation: The migrated record preserves the source metadata, timestamps, ownership, and existing trace links or classifications where mapping is clean, with those details visible in the imported record.

setup: A policy document is being imported and one trace link or field in the source file cannot be matched to a target value automatically.
action: The user completes the import process for the document.
expected_observation: The system retains the original unresolved value, marks the field or link for review, and surfaces it in the import review results rather than overwriting or discarding it.

setup: An analyst has uploaded a security requirements spreadsheet into the import wizard, and the file contains columns for source ID, control name, owner, and trace links.
action: The analyst steps through the guided import process, matches each incoming column to a target field, reviews the preview of the parsed rows, and proceeds with the import while one required link is intentionally left unmapped.
expected_observation: The system displays a field-matching screen and a row preview before commit, highlights the unmapped required link, and prevents final import until the missing link is resolved or explicitly acknowledged for review.

setup: A validated import file has been uploaded into the project, and the live project currently contains published requirements and traceability records.
action: The analyst completes the import and submits it for publication.
expected_observation: The imported records are first stored in a staging area, and only after successful validation are they published into the live project; no partially imported data appears directly in the live workspace.

setup: The project contains imported items with one unresolved trace link to a policy reference that could not be matched automatically.
action: The analyst opens the import review queue without confirming the unresolved item.
expected_observation: The unmatched item remains visible in the review queue with its broken link status preserved, and it is not removed from review until a user confirms or resolves it.

setup: A user is watching a security policy and its linked requirements, and notification preferences for review alerts are enabled.
action: Another analyst updates the related policy text or changes a trace link that affects the watched item.
expected_observation: The watcher receives a review alert or notification indicating that the related policy, requirement, or trace link was updated and needs attention.

setup: An existing mapping between an imported control and an internal requirement has prior history entries stored in the system.
action: The analyst changes the mapping from one source value to another and saves the update.
expected_observation: The system preserves the previous link history and shows an audit trail identifying what mapping changed, including the old and new association.

setup: A mapped field currently has an approved value, and the analyst is reviewing a proposed remapping to a different source value.
action: The analyst opens the comparison view for the mapping change.
expected_observation: The system presents a before-and-after comparison showing the original value alongside the new proposed or saved value so the analyst can assess the change.

setup: A requirement item was imported from a source file and later one of its attributes was manually edited by an analyst.
action: The analyst views the item details and trace status in the workspace.
expected_observation: The system clearly distinguishes inherited imported data from manually corrected data, showing which fields still come from the import and which fields were changed by hand.

setup: An automated mapping job is processing a batch of imported requirements, and the source file structure has changed since the last successful import, causing column positions to shift.
action: The automation attempts to apply the existing mapping rules to the changed file structure.
expected_observation: The system stops the automation, flags the affected set for human review, and marks the mapping as unreliable due to the structural change or contextual mismatch.

setup: A batch update is running against imported security controls, and the source records have already been staged for replacement.
action: An unexpected failure occurs during automatic mapping or batch update before the commit completes.
expected_observation: The system preserves the original source data and previously committed values, does not overwrite them with partial changes, and leaves the failed batch in a recoverable error state.

setup: The workspace contains several pending updates, including one tied to a legal compliance obligation, one tied to a security control, and one routine editorial change.
action: The analyst opens the prioritized update list.
expected_observation: The system surfaces the high-priority compliance- and security-related updates first, especially those affecting multiple requirements, ahead of lower-impact routine changes.

setup: A set of proposed changes is pending review, including items with varying numbers of linked requirements and different levels of traceability risk.
action: The analyst inspects the change summary for each pending item.
expected_observation: Each item shows impact counts, urgency, and an indicator of whether the change breaks existing traceability, enabling the analyst to rank the updates appropriately.

setup: The workspace contains imported items that have been flagged by the system due to conflicts, unresolved links, or incomplete mapping.
action: The analyst opens the project workspace and filters to pending issues.
expected_observation: Flagged items appear directly in the workspace with clear statuses such as needs review, conflicting mapping, or unresolved import, making them visible without searching outside the workspace.

setup: A flagged mapping item has an original source value, an attempted suggested mapping, and a rejection reason captured during import.
action: The analyst opens the item's details panel.
expected_observation: The system displays the original source value, the suggested mapping if available, and the reason the mapping was rejected or left ambiguous.

setup: An analyst is reviewing a flagged item that has competing candidate mappings and an unresolved import conflict.
action: The analyst opens the item, compares the candidate values, selects the correct mapping or chooses escalation, and saves the decision.
expected_observation: The selected mapping is recorded or the item is marked for escalation, and the decision is persisted with the item's review state updated accordingly.

setup: A conflict resolution workflow is active for an imported item that requires analyst judgment.
action: The analyst resolves the conflict and submits the decision with supporting reasoning or evidence notes.
expected_observation: The system logs the identity of the person who made the decision, the timestamp of the decision, and the evidence or reasoning used to justify it.

setup: A requirement item in the current project has one or more open trace links to related goals, policies, and downstream requirements, and the item is currently marked as unresolved.
action: The reviewer records a resolution for the item and confirms the resolution in the item details view.
expected_observation: The item status changes to resolved, the related trace links are updated to reflect the resolution, and the updated link state is visible in the traceability view.

setup: A requirement item has just been resolved, and the project audit history is available to authorized reviewers.
action: The reviewer opens the resolved item and requests its history or audit trail.
expected_observation: The system shows the previous unresolved state and the resolution transition in the audit history, while preserving the resolved item as the current state.

setup: A conflict has been resolved for a requirement, and at least one downstream item is impacted by the resolution.
action: The reviewer completes the conflict handling action.
expected_observation: A notification or activity feed entry appears stating that the conflict has been handled, and it identifies the affected downstream items.

setup: A user signs into an active project with recent items, unresolved conflicts, and pending review tasks available.
action: The user opens the application home screen or project dashboard.
expected_observation: A dashboard-style interface is displayed with quick access to the current project, a list of recent items, unresolved conflicts, and review tasks.

setup: The project contains goals, requirements, policies, and trace links across multiple items.
action: The user enters a search term and applies a filter to narrow results by item type or trace relationship.
expected_observation: Relevant goals, requirements, policies, and trace links are returned quickly, and the filter selection meaningfully reduces the displayed results without requiring manual navigation through each section.

setup: The user is editing a requirement that follows a standard project template and includes fields suitable for autocomplete and inline updates.
action: The user starts creating a new item from a template, selects an autocomplete suggestion, and edits a field directly in the list or detail panel.
expected_observation: The template pre-populates expected fields, autocomplete suggestions appear while typing, and inline edits are accepted without opening a separate full edit form.

setup: The user is editing project content while the network connection is unstable or temporarily unavailable.
action: The user changes a requirement field and then pauses before leaving the screen.
expected_observation: The system automatically saves the change when possible, shows clear feedback that the content has not yet synced if the save is pending, and retains the edited value on screen.

setup: A user has items in three different save states: one fully synced, one waiting to sync, and one with a failed sync attempt.
action: The user views the item list or detail screen where these changes are shown.
expected_observation: Each item displays a clear status indicator distinguishing saved, pending sync, and failed sync states.

setup: A user was working in the application when the browser closed unexpectedly or the session was interrupted before manual logout.
action: The user returns to the application and signs in again.
expected_observation: The system restores the interrupted session state or offers recovery of the unfinished work so the user can resume from the last meaningful point.

setup: The application is opened on a typical project with several items loaded and the device is within normal operating conditions.
action: The user navigates between the dashboard, item details, and search results while opening and editing records.
expected_observation: Screens remain responsive, avoid visibly heavy page loads, and do not rely on long full-page refreshes for routine navigation or updates.

setup: The user is viewing a project page with a list of requirements and a side panel or details pane visible.
action: The user edits one requirement field and saves or autosaves the change.
expected_observation: Only the affected portion of the screen updates, such as the edited field, status badge, or detail pane, rather than the entire page reloading.

setup: The connection becomes slow or high-latency while the user is viewing a project with important summary information.
action: The user opens the dashboard or navigates to a project overview during the slow connection.
expected_observation: The most important project information remains accessible, such as current project name, recent items, unresolved conflicts, or key counts, even if secondary content loads more slowly.

setup: A new user opens the application for the first time in a fresh account or first-use state.
action: The user lands on the application home screen and accepts or starts the onboarding experience.
expected_observation: A guided first-use walkthrough appears and introduces the core areas of the product instead of leaving the user without orientation.

setup: The first-use walkthrough is active for a new user who has not yet learned the project workflow.
action: The user advances through the walkthrough steps.
expected_observation: The walkthrough explains how goals, policies, and requirements connect, and it demonstrates the main workflow of creating or opening a project, adding a goal or requirement, linking it back to a policy, and reviewing traceability.

setup: The user is on a screen where a form, list, or editor contains fields that may need guidance.
action: The user pauses over a field label, help icon, or contextual hint trigger within the screen.
expected_observation: A short in-screen help message appears with relevant guidance for that context, without taking the user away from the current task.

setup: A new analyst signs in for the first time and opens the home page of the Security and Privacy Requirements Analysis Tool with no existing projects.
action: The analyst starts a new project from the onboarding flow.
expected_observation: The system presents at least one sample project or starter template, such as a prefilled security assessment or privacy review project, that the analyst can open and use as a starting point.

setup: A first-time user is viewing the interactive onboarding walkthrough in a fresh account with no prior training completed.
action: The user follows the walkthrough and completes the first small guided example, then attempts to continue past the example steps.
expected_observation: The user can complete a short hands-on example within the walkthrough, and the walkthrough ends or offers a clear skip/exit option without trapping the user in a long mandatory tutorial.

setup: A new user opens a project for the first time and is about to view classification labels, compliance fields, and a comparison view for the first time.
action: The user hovers over or opens each of these unfamiliar fields and views them in context.
expected_observation: The system displays plain-language explanations for the classification, compliance, and comparison elements using understandable wording that describes what the field means and how it should be used.

setup: A new user begins onboarding in a project where autosave and synchronization are enabled.
action: The user reaches the first steps of the onboarding flow and edits a field that triggers saving behavior.
expected_observation: The onboarding explains early that changes are autosaved and synced, and the user sees a clear status indicator describing when content is saved locally, synced, or still updating.

setup: A user is editing a project while the network connection is active and autosave is enabled.
action: The connection drops during an edit and the system attempts to save or sync the change.
expected_observation: The system shows a clear recovery message telling the user that the connection was lost, that work is محفوظ/retained, and that syncing will resume when the connection returns.

setup: A user experiences a synchronization failure or temporary recovery issue while working on a project.
action: The system reports the sync or recovery problem to the user.
expected_observation: The message uses plain, non-technical language and avoids vague warnings or jargon, instead stating what happened and what the user should do next in simple terms.

setup: Two collaborators are working on the same analysis project, and one collaborator makes changes to a section already open in another user's browser.
action: The second collaborator views the project after the first collaborator saves changes.
expected_observation: The other user's view updates to show the collaboration changes in a reviewable way without requiring a full page reload, and the changed content is presented clearly for review.

setup: A very large project with many records, controls, and comparison items is opened by a user on a standard workstation.
action: The user opens the project and scrolls through the content or navigates to additional sections.
expected_observation: The system loads content incrementally in visible portions rather than rendering the entire project at once, and the user can begin working before all data has finished loading.

setup: Two users are editing different parts of the same project at the same time, including a sensitive analysis section that is visible to both under their permissions.
action: Both users make overlapping edits and save their changes during the same session.
expected_observation: The system does not lock either user out, both users remain able to work concurrently, and the resulting edits are shown and reconciled cleanly with any conflicts surfaced for review instead of silently overwriting work.

setup: The organization has multiple projects, including one large, data-heavy project and several smaller active projects used by other teams.
action: A user opens a smaller project while the large project is being loaded or edited by another user.
expected_observation: The smaller project opens without noticeable slowdown caused by the large project, demonstrating that projects remain isolated enough that one heavy project does not degrade the responsiveness of others.

setup: A user has just entered a project that contains a large amount of analysis data, and the project has not fully finished loading.
action: The user opens a commonly used view such as the project overview, recent changes, or a frequently used summary screen.
expected_observation: The requested common view appears quickly without waiting for the entire project to finish loading, allowing the user to begin reading or navigating immediately.

setup: A user is actively viewing or editing a project and the network connection becomes unstable or disconnects completely.
action: The disconnect occurs while the user remains on the page.
expected_observation: The system handles the disconnect gracefully by keeping the interface understandable, preserving the user's current work state, and showing a recovery path rather than crashing or showing a blank failure screen.

setup: A user enters text into an unsaved analysis field and the connection is working normally at the start of the edit.
action: The connection drops temporarily before the user can complete the save.
expected_observation: The user's entered work is not lost, the system retains the draft or pending change, and the content is restored or synchronized once connectivity returns.

setup: The organization has not approved public cloud deployment for the Security and Privacy Requirements Analysis Tool.
action: An administrator attempts to deploy or start the system outside the managed organizational environment, such as in a public cloud target.
expected_observation: The system does not proceed with public cloud deployment and instead remains deployed in the organization's managed environment unless public cloud approval has been explicitly granted.

setup: A project contains sensitive analysis content, and users with different roles such as analyst, reviewer, and viewer are signed into the system.
action: A user without the required role attempts to edit sensitive content or open a restricted work item, while an authorized user performs the same action.
expected_observation: The unauthorized user is prevented from editing or viewing restricted content, while the authorized user can access the content according to role-based permissions.

setup: An artifact in the analysis workspace is in Approved status and a standard analyst account is viewing it. The workspace also contains version history for the artifact, and an administrator account with reopen permission is available.
action: The analyst attempts to edit the approved artifact without creating a new version, then the administrator attempts to reopen the same artifact for editing.
expected_observation: The analyst is prevented from modifying the approved artifact and is shown that editing is locked on approved content. The administrator is allowed to reopen the artifact or create an editable state, and any subsequent edits are recorded as a new version rather than altering the approved version directly.

setup: The system is displaying a validation result for an import or analysis action where the input is syntactically valid but contains a non-blocking inconsistency, and another case where the input is clearly invalid, such as a required source file being missing or a field containing an impossible value.
action: A user submits both the non-blocking inconsistent input and the clearly invalid input through the same workflow.
expected_observation: The clearly invalid input produces a hard error that stops the action and explains what is not allowed. The non-blocking inconsistency does not trigger a hard error; instead it is presented as a reviewable warning or note so the user can continue investigating.

setup: An artifact has at least one approved older version and a newer working version exists in the system. Audit access is enabled for the project.
action: A user opens the artifact history and accesses the approved older version while viewing the latest version separately.
expected_observation: The approved older version remains available in the audit trail with its original content intact. The newer work does not overwrite the approved version, and the system clearly distinguishes each version by version number, timestamp, and approval state.

setup: A file import has loaded requirements or source documents into the staging area, and the imported records are not yet published to the live project.
action: A reviewer opens the staged imported items and completes the review/approval step before publishing them.
expected_observation: The imported data stays in staging until review is completed. The system blocks publication to the live project until a review decision is recorded, and only reviewed items become available in the live project.

setup: An import job is processing a source document where the mapping engine detects multiple possible target fields or a context mismatch that prevents confident assignment.
action: The user starts the import and the system encounters an ambiguous or contextually incorrect mapping for one or more imported items.
expected_observation: Automation stops for the affected items or import step, and the system requests human review instead of auto-applying the mapping. The ambiguous source value and the conflicting mapping options are presented for manual resolution.

setup: The analysis workspace contains a prioritized queue with items tagged at different compliance and project risk levels, including high-risk and low-risk items.
action: The user opens the prioritized list or queue view for analysis work.
expected_observation: Items with higher compliance risk or project risk appear ahead of lower-risk items. The ordering clearly favors higher-risk items so they are surfaced first for attention and action.

setup: A project contains analysis artifacts ready for transfer, and the system has export options enabled for at least one common file format and import options for the same or equivalent format.
action: The user exports the artifacts to a common format and then imports a file in a supported common format into the project.
expected_observation: The export produces a usable file in a standard format, and the import accepts the supported format without requiring a custom adapter. The imported content appears in the workspace with its key fields preserved.

setup: The system is connected to a document repository that contains relevant source documents, and the user has permission to browse that repository.
action: The user selects documents from the repository and imports them into the analysis workspace.
expected_observation: The system retrieves the selected repository documents and brings them into the workspace or staging area. The source repository location is retained as provenance information for the imported items.

setup: An external issue-tracking system contains issues related to a project item, and a link or sync connection has been configured between the two systems.
action: The user links an analysis item to an issue-tracking item and then updates the basic status of the issue in the issue tracker.
expected_observation: The analysis item shows the external issue linkage, and the basic status information is reflected in the analysis workspace according to the sync rules. The user can see that the analysis item is associated with the external tracker record.

setup: A user prepares migration inputs in a spreadsheet, a Word document, and an exported requirement database file, all containing source requirements and related metadata.
action: The user uploads the structured documents as migration inputs.
expected_observation: The system accepts the spreadsheet, Word file, and exported database input as supported migration sources. The extracted requirements and metadata are placed into the migration flow without requiring manual re-entry of every record.

setup: Legacy documents, analyses, and traceability records are available for migration from an older project, and the destination project includes a staging area.
action: The user imports the legacy materials into the new project through the migration process.
expected_observation: The system stores the imported legacy content in the staging area rather than publishing it directly. The staged records preserve the imported analyses and traceability links so they can be reviewed before promotion.

setup: An imported item arrives with a source value that cannot be automatically mapped to a target field, and the original source text is still available in the import record.
action: The user opens the imported item that failed automatic mapping.
expected_observation: The system displays the original source value exactly as it appeared in the import. The unmapped value remains visible for review instead of being discarded or replaced with blank content.

setup: An imported item has one or more suggested target mappings generated by the import engine, and the import review screen is available.
action: The user opens the import review screen for the item.
expected_observation: The system shows the suggested mapping alongside the imported source item. The reviewer can see the proposed target field or destination before deciding whether to accept or change it.

setup: A user is performing an analysis on a project with a moderate number of source documents and requirements, using the standard workspace tools available to normal users.
action: The user completes a typical analysis flow, including importing sources, reviewing mappings, and linking requirements to policies.
expected_observation: The analysis can be completed within a streamlined workflow with minimal unnecessary navigation or repeated manual steps. The user reaches the analysis result faster than a separate manual review process and does not encounter avoidable delays in common tasks.

setup: A project contains requirements, source policies, and an active traceability view that highlights unmatched or weakly linked items.
action: The user runs traceability analysis and reviews the resulting coverage report.
expected_observation: The system surfaces missing traces between requirements and source policies so they are easy to identify and close. The report highlights unlinked or partially linked items, helping the user reduce trace gaps during review.

setup: A security analyst is reviewing a completed requirements analysis project with several trace links already created between policies, requirements, and test evidence.
action: The analyst opens the built-in validation and compliance review view before submitting the project for formal review.
expected_observation: The system highlights missing traces, inconsistent labels, and unresolved policy mappings within the workspace, allowing the analyst to correct issues before final review or compliance checking.

setup: Two analysts are working on the same privacy assessment template and both have access to the same set of requirement categories and tagging conventions.
action: Each analyst independently classifies the same sample artifact set and assigns trace links using the standard workflow.
expected_observation: The system presents the same controlled vocabulary, category options, and link types to both analysts, and the resulting classifications are aligned rather than using different labels or structures.

setup: The system contains a large enterprise workspace with many users, multiple projects, thousands of artifacts, and a dense network of trace links.
action: A user opens the project dashboard, searches for an artifact, and navigates between linked items in the large workspace.
expected_observation: The dashboard, search results, and trace navigation remain responsive and usable without noticeable sluggishness, even at high data volume.

setup: An analyst is connected through a slow VPN link with intermittent latency and reduced bandwidth while accessing the system remotely.
action: The analyst signs in, opens a project, and edits an artifact while the connection remains unstable.
expected_observation: The interface continues to function in a usable way, with requests completing successfully when possible and without the application becoming unusable due to the slow or unstable remote connection.

setup: The organization has single sign-on enabled and role-based access rules defining different permissions for analysts, reviewers, and administrators.
action: A user signs in through the corporate identity provider and attempts to access project functions that are outside their assigned role.
expected_observation: The system authenticates through single sign-on and allows only the actions permitted by the user's role, while blocking unauthorized access to restricted functions and data.

setup: The system contains sensitive internal project data, and audit logging plus restricted storage policies are enabled.
action: A user opens a sensitive artifact, modifies a trace link, and then signs out.
expected_observation: The access, change, and sign-out events are recorded in the audit trail, and the sensitive data remains stored in a protected manner consistent with internal security controls.

setup: An analyst is actively working in a project while the network periodically slows down and the session is approaching its timeout threshold.
action: The analyst continues editing an artifact and navigates across several views during the degraded connection period.
expected_observation: The application remains usable despite slow responses, warns the user when the session is nearing timeout, and preserves the current work state during the unstable period.

setup: An analyst has unsaved edits in a project artifact and the system is configured to handle brief connection interruptions.
action: The network connection drops temporarily while the analyst is editing the artifact and then reconnects shortly afterward.
expected_observation: The analyst does not lose the unsaved work; the edited content is retained or restored after reconnection, and the system clearly indicates the recovery status.

setup: A user opens the main application home page on a standard desktop browser with no other overlays or dialogs present.
action: The user scans the dashboard, opens a project, and moves between primary screens.
expected_observation: The interface appears uncluttered, loads quickly, and presents the main controls and content in a clean, lightweight layout that remains responsive to navigation.

setup: An analyst is entering new requirements into a project that already contains related artifacts and prior classifications.
action: The analyst makes a common input mistake such as leaving a required field blank or selecting an inconsistent artifact type and then continues editing.
expected_observation: The system provides clear guidance, allows the analyst to correct the mistake without restarting the workflow, and supports a low-friction recovery path with minimal disruption.

setup: A project contains several artifacts that share common metadata such as owner, source system, and policy category.
action: The analyst creates a new artifact and then adds several similar items using the project's standard entry workflow.
expected_observation: The system reuses previously entered values through defaults, templates, or copy-forward behavior where appropriate, reducing repeated manual data entry.

setup: The workspace contains a large dataset with many artifacts, numerous tags, and a dense set of trace links between items.
action: The analyst runs a search, applies multiple filters, compares two artifacts, and opens cross-references from a selected requirement.
expected_observation: Search, filtering, comparison, and cross-reference navigation complete quickly and remain practical to use even at large scale.

setup: A project has grown to include a high number of artifacts, categories, and linked records, increasing the amount of information displayed in the interface.
action: The analyst opens the project overview and scrolls through artifact lists and linked-item panels.
expected_observation: The interface stays readable and usable, avoids overcrowding the screen, and organizes high artifact volumes without overwhelming the analyst with clutter.

setup: A synchronization attempt is interrupted by a network issue and a recovery operation is required to restore the latest changes.
action: The analyst views the sync status area after the interruption and inspects any recovery prompt.
expected_observation: The system shows clear status labels and plain-language messages that explain the sync failure and the recovery action needed, without technical jargon.

setup: The analyst has a project that contains several low-severity flagged items that do not require immediate interruption of work.
action: The system generates alerts for those minor flagged items during the user's normal workflow.
expected_observation: The system presents the minor items in a digest or summary view instead of repeatedly interrupting the analyst with excessive individual notifications.

setup: An analyst is reviewing security and privacy requirements in the collaboration workspace, with the related item open and team discussion channels enabled inside the system.
action: The analyst adds a comment, assigns a follow-up task to another analyst, and @mentions a colleague on the requirement without leaving the application.
expected_observation: The comment, task assignment, and mention are recorded and visible in the workspace activity stream, and the analyst can continue collaborating inside the system without being redirected to email.

setup: Two analysts are viewing related requirements that share the same policy traceability links, and both have edit access to overlapping fields.
action: One analyst begins editing a trace link while the second analyst updates the related requirement at the same time and attempts to save.
expected_observation: The system detects the overlapping edit, warns the second analyst before finalizing the save, and prevents silent overwriting until the conflict is reviewed.

setup: A requirement record contains a trace link to a policy that has already been deleted, or a previously valid trace relationship is now broken.
action: An analyst opens the requirement in the traceability view or attempts to follow the broken link.
expected_observation: The system flags the missing or broken trace relationship, clearly identifies the affected record, and keeps the requirement recoverable for later repair or restoration.

setup: An analyst is editing a requirement or analysis record in an active session with unsaved changes present.
action: The network connection drops or the session is interrupted before the analyst saves and exits the record.
expected_observation: The system preserves the in-progress work, restores it when the analyst reconnects or signs in again, and presents recovery guidance indicating how to resume the interrupted work.

setup: A batch update or automatic mapping job is running against a set of requirements and trace links, with original source data still available.
action: The update process fails unexpectedly during execution.
expected_observation: The system leaves the original data unchanged, marks the affected items or batch as requiring human review, and does not substitute guessed mappings or partial automated changes as final results.

setup: An imported requirement or mapping cannot be matched confidently because the source text is ambiguous or the target relationship has multiple plausible candidates.
action: The analyst imports the item or reviews the ambiguous mapping result.
expected_observation: The ambiguous item remains visible in a review queue, is not auto-approved or hidden, and stays there until an analyst confirms or resolves it.

setup: A requirement or artifact has been archived and is no longer part of the active working set.
action: An analyst opens the archive view, inspects the archived artifact, and follows its trace links.
expected_observation: The archived artifact can still be viewed and traced, and it is clearly labeled as archived so it is not mistaken for an active current requirement.

setup: The deployment planning record is open for SPRAT, and the hosting section is awaiting confirmation from IT.
action: A project administrator reviews the hosting decision field and attempts to finalize the deployment configuration.
expected_observation: The system shows the hosting setup as unconfirmed or pending IT approval, and the administrator cannot treat the hosting arrangement as a finalized requirement.

setup: The integration planning area is open, with no approved list of external systems for direct SPRAT integration.
action: An analyst attempts to define or enable direct integration targets for SPRAT.
expected_observation: The system indicates that the direct external system integrations are not yet confirmed and keeps the integration scope open for later decision rather than locking in unsupported targets.

setup: The project dashboard includes KPI tracking placeholders for analysis time reduction, error reduction, and compliance improvement.
action: A manager reviews the KPI definitions and tries to compare them against target values.
expected_observation: The system shows the KPI targets as undefined or pending approval, and no false numeric target is presented as an agreed acceptance threshold.

setup: A migration preparation workspace is open, but the list of legacy file or data formats to be supported has not been confirmed.
action: An analyst begins planning a migration import and selects supported source formats.
expected_observation: The system marks legacy format support as unresolved and does not claim compatibility for specific formats until the migration scope is approved.

setup: The offline usage settings are available in the application preferences, and the product decision on full offline editing has not been made.
action: A user opens the offline editing configuration or attempts to switch the product into full offline edit mode.
expected_observation: The system shows full offline editing as undecided or unavailable pending confirmation, and it does not advertise full offline editing as a committed capability.

setup: Deployment options are being reviewed for SPRAT, and public cloud approval has not yet been granted.
action: A release manager attempts to select a public cloud hosting option for the deployment plan.
expected_observation: The system indicates that public cloud deployment is conditional on specific approval and does not allow it to be treated as an approved deployment choice until that approval is recorded.
